title: Evidence provenance and content identity
content: Evidence provenance records a title, source reference, publisher or origin, publication date, and version where supplied. A cryptographic content hash identifies canonical text and can detect a content change relative to a known digest. It does not authenticate a publisher or establish that the text is correct. Retrieval scores indicate similarity to a query, not clinical authority. A fictional evidence card can retain these source fields through chunking and search. Provenance supports tracing a passage back to its document. Clinical validity requires separate assessment outside this retrieval experiment. Synthetic research evidence only. Retrieval relevance != clinical validity.
